cues: Curtis called it a necessary evil.
A better way to put it: it is the price of opening the stomata to let carbon dioxide in.
The same pore serves both, so a plant loses hundreds of water molecules for every carbon dioxide it fixes.
In return it gets a cooler leaf and a stream that carries minerals up.
